stage_a.note: Upbeat, energetic delivery with smiles and engaged interaction throughout the pitch.
Sustained engagement and excitement about the product's features and how it works.
Friendly, highly approachable mother-daughter dynamic, sharing high-fives and smiles.

venture.description: Silicone products for kids, including ergonomic marker holders, bath scrubbers, and reusable straws.

turns.speaker: F1, F2
turns.summary: Amy and Marlo present the Marker Parker, explaining how it stops markers from rolling away and drying out.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks Marlo if she made the drawings shown on the presentation boards.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo confirms she made the drawings and that the words are quotes from the investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori compliments Marlo on her drawing skills.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark jokes about discovering he is bald from his portrait.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin reads the quote on his portrait about pairing up with people whose strengths compensate for weaknesses.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks Marlo how old she is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo states she is seven and a half years old.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori expresses being impressed by Marlo's young age.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo invites the panel to try out the Marker Parker themselves.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma agrees to try the product.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks whether they are selling the markers along with the holder or just the holder.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy clarifies that they are only selling the base holder.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark confirms that the product is just a holder.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo agrees that it is a holder.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma asks if the holder works for any type of pen or marker.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy explains it works for broad tips but they are modifying it to fit fine tips as well.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks what prevents a large marker manufacturer from copying the idea.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy explains they filed a provisional patent and that Marlo thought of the idea a year ago.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma expresses surprise and admiration that Marlo invented the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma asks what the retail price of the holder is.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo states the product sells for fifteen dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks what it costs to manufacture the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy states the landed cost to make the holder is $2.71.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert compliments the strong profit margin on the product.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma asks how they are currently marketing and selling the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy explains the business started six years ago with a different product, a towel.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin asks if they want to show the panel some of their other products.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo demonstrates the ScrubBEE, a silicone scrubber for kids.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if they also manufacture the silicone straw shown on the table.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy explains the Build-a-Straw product and how it comes apart for cleaning.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma asks which item is their hero product and what their sales are.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy states the scrubber is the hero product and they did $230,000 in sales last year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks to clarify if the $230,000 was just for the scrubber.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy clarifies it was for the whole business, but the scrubber accounted for 80% of sales despite lost inventory.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if they made a profit or lost money on last year's sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy states they grossed $97,000 and made a small profit, asking not to discuss the current year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks what happened with their sales in the current year.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma encourages Amy to share the current year's numbers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy states they have done $110,000 so far this year without the scrubber in stock.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert asks if they are making any money on this year's sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy admits she lost $77,000 this year and explains she invested $100,000 of her own money.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin praises Marlo for holding the floor so well at seven years old.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy thanks Kevin and agrees that Marlo is phenomenal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin exits, citing fear of the numbers and too many problems in the business model.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy playfully suggests Kevin might want to take his decision back.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Kevin agrees to wait and see what else they have.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy demonstrates their next product, a silicone food container.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma asks if the product is a silicone sandwich storage container.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy confirms it is a sandwich container.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark challenges Amy, saying she has inventitis and needs to solve current problems instead of inventing new products.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy defends the new product by stating it has already generated $8,500 in sales.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark asks how many units of the new product have been sold.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Marlo answers that they have sold over a thousand units.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Mark exits, reiterating his concern over her lack of focus on existing products.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori asks Amy if she is running the business completely alone.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy indicates she is not alone, pointing to Marlo as her support.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Lori exits, feeling Amy is overextended and needs to focus on making one product successful.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emma exits, stating she admires them but finds the business approach too scatterbrained to invest in.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Robert exits, advising them to operate as a design studio rather than a product company due to lack of focus.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Amy thanks the panel for their time and feedback.

decisions.note: Fear of numbers, wants to pour gas on a working model, too many problems in this business.
Inventitis, losing money, needs to solve current inventory problems first.
Overextended in every way, should focus on making one product a huge success.
Approach feels scatterbrained, not something she can invest in.
Needs laser focus, showed too many products, suggests they act as a design studio instead.
